thread: Elena: Dropping a fresh mock for the usage summary: a compact sparkline + mini-metric row (total spend, tokens, avg latency) and a small expander to reveal per-project token rows. Main questions: should the org/project toggle live in the left rail, top bar, or inside the metric row? And what should the export CTA read (Download invoice vs Export billing)? Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/new-usage-spark (page 'Compact Summary / Sparkline'). Marcus: Love the sparkline for quick scanning. For discoverability the org/project scope should be visually close to the Export CTA so users immediately understand what they'll get when exporting. My vote: keep scope pill left of the metric row, Export on the right of the same row (so it's one horizontal band). Tariq: Implementation note: expandable per-project rows can be heavy for customers with 200+ projects. We should default to top-5 + "Show all" which triggers virtualization. Also, server should return collapsed aggregates to avoid client-side summation on initial load. Sophie: Copy nit: "Export billing" reads more product-y and covers multiple formats. Suggest: button label "Export billing (CSV)" with caret for other formats. Default action should start CSV download and show a non-blocking toast: "Billing export generating — link available here". Menu items: "CSV (rollup)", "CSV (per-project)", "PDF (zipped)". Show ETA for PDF. Elena: Agree on CTA. Also want explicit token labeling: currently label is "Tokens" which confuses some customers. Propose "Token units (request+response)" and a question-mark tooltip linking to docs. Tooltip must be accessible via keyboard. Marcus: Chart accessibility: sparkline needs an accessible label and a summary. Example SR piece: Spend sparkline for Acme Corp: last 30 days, peak on Apr 12, total $12,345. And per-data-point focusable points with aria-labels like "Apr 12: $1234 (120k tokens)". Tariq: Backend export endpoints: we'll provide /exports/rollup.csv, /exports/per-project.csv (streaming), and /exports/pdf (queued). Each response will include a request_id header for tracing. We'll also return pricing_version so clients can show "pricing as of v12". Sophie: UX edge: when multi-project scope is selected, what does CSV mean? Default to rollup, but include an explicit "Per-project CSV" menu item (zipped if large). In menu copy, make that obvious: "Per-project CSV (zipped)". Also telemetry: emit events export.click with {format, scope, date_range}. Elena: a11y-bot can you run contrast + keyboard nav checks on the compact row and export menu? We need focus outlines on the sparkline points and ensure the export menu is reachable and announces scope/date. export-bot: export-service queued on branch feature/compact-sparkline. Preview: https://staging.redwood.ai/preview/741. Exports endpoints stubbed. Tariq: Quick CSV header suggestion for rollup: ``` date,scope_type,scope_id,total_usd,total_tokens,pricing_version,request_id 2026-03-01,org,acme,412.34,1234567,v12,rq_abc123 ``` This keeps machine parsing easy and includes metadata. a11y-bot: queued scan for feature/compact-sparkline. Preliminary findings: export button missing aria-haspopup, sparkline points are not keyboard focusable, tooltip not reachable via keyboard on some themes. Recommend: add role=\"menu\" to dropdown, make SVG points
